extra.message: Privilege escalation via self-registration role field — Unauthenticated attacker can create an account with property_admin or property_manager role, bypassing the intended privilege hierarchy and gaining full administrative access to tenants, leases, payments, and documents. [verified: register() at auth.py:26 assigns role directly from client-supplied UserCreate.role with no server-side restriction, letting anonymous callers self-assign PROPERTY_ADMIN or PROPERTY_MANAGER.]

Sensitive internal ops router protected only by static shared-secret header — If the static token leaks (logs, source, config) any anonymous caller gets RCE-equivalent capability across the whole ops surface [verified: Duplicate of idx 12 — entire /ops/* router (including pickle RCE, command injection, XXE, SSRF, mongo passthrough) gated only by a static header equality check with no per-user auth.]

Sensitive internal operations gated only by static shared header token — Bypass of proper authentication/authorization for RCE-capable endpoints if the static token is compromised [verified: _wrk_gate is a single static string-compare header check guarding pickle/RCE/command-injection endpoints instead of real per-user auth/authz.]

Pickle deserialization of untrusted data — Remote code execution via crafted pickle payload [verified: pickle.loads() runs directly on raw/base64-decoded request body with only the static header gate; no validation of content.]

Server-side template injection via Jinja2 — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape / SSTI payload [verified: Template('Result: ' + fragment).render() builds and renders a template from unsanitized user input, enabling SSTI/RCE.]
OS command injection via host parameter — Arbitrary shell command execution on the server [verified: Duplicate of idx 1 — unsanitized host concatenated into os.system shell command.]

Server-side template injection in ops jinja endpoint — Arbitrary code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape payloads [verified: Duplicate of idx 4 — Jinja2 Template built and rendered from concatenated user fragment.]

Insecure pickle deserialization in ops endpoint — Remote code execution via crafted pickle payload [verified: Duplicate of idx 0 — pickle.loads on attacker-controlled bytes behind only the static token gate.]

Missing property-scope check on CSV payment import allows cross-tenant writes — A property manager can create/modify payment records for tenants and leases outside their assigned properties, corrupting financial records belonging to other tenants/managers. [verified: import_payments allows PROPERTY_MANAGER role and directly inserts tenant_id/lease_id from CSV rows into PaymentRecord with zero check against get_managed_property_ids or any tenant/lease ownership validation, unlike scoped endpoints elsewhere in the codebase.]

IDOR on message retrieval endpoint — Any authenticated non-tenant user (e.g. a maintenance worker) can read arbitrary private messages and internal notes between other users/tenants they have no relationship to, exposing sensitive communications. [verified: get_message only restricts TENANT role; MAINTENANCE_WORKER and any other role can fetch any message by ID including internal notes with no participant/property scoping.]

IDOR on message replies endpoint — Any authenticated user can read reply threads of conversations they are not part of, leaking private tenant/manager communications. [verified: list_replies filters by parent_id only, stripping internal notes solely for TENANT role, so any authenticated non-tenant (and even tenants for non-internal replies) can read reply threads they aren't part of.]

Sensitive data (auth header, raw body) written to logs — Credential/PII leakage to anyone with log access [verified: logger.warning logs raw body and Authorization header verbatim, persisting bearer tokens/PII into logs.]
Sensitive data (auth header) written to logs — Credential/token exposure to anyone with log access [verified: Duplicate of idx 11 — Authorization header and raw body logged verbatim.]

Path traversal and plaintext PII write in ops vault endpoint — Arbitrary file write via traversal and plaintext storage of SSN/card data [verified: Duplicate of idx 8 — path traversal via ref plus plaintext SSN/card storage.]

Plaintext storage of SSN/card data and path traversal via ref — Persistent plaintext exposure of PII/financial data on disk; combined with traversal, write to arbitrary paths [verified: ref used unsanitized in BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' (path traversal) and SSN/card written in plaintext with no encryption.]

SSRF via arbitrary endpoint fetch — Access to internal-only services, cloud metadata endpoints, or port scanning of internal network [verified: urllib.request.urlopen on caller-supplied endpoint with no allow-list, response body returned to caller — classic SSRF.]

SSRF via ops relay endpoint — Access to internal-only services/metadata endpoints, port scanning, response exfiltration [verified: Duplicate of idx 3 — unrestricted SSRF via urlopen on caller-supplied endpoint.]
NoSQL injection via Mongo ops query passthrough — Unauthorized data access or query-based DoS/RCE via $where [verified: Duplicate of idx 5 — unsanitized Mongo filter passthrough to find_one().]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized MongoDB filter — Unauthorized data access/exfiltration from MongoDB collection, potential server-side JS execution via $where [verified: payload.get('filter', payload) passed unmodified to find_one(), allowing NoSQL operator injection.]

Path traversal via arbitrary file write in ops dock endpoint — Arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory, potentially overwriting application files [verified: Duplicate of idx 7 — arbitrary file write via unsanitized name parameter.]
XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure and SSRF via XML external entities [verified: Duplicate of idx 2 — XXE-enabled lxml parser on attacker body.]

Password reset token disclosed via application logs — An attacker with log/console access can harvest valid password-reset tokens for any user and take over their account without needing email access. [verified: password_reset_request prints the live reset JWT to stdout via print(), which is captured by container/log aggregation, exposing a valid account-takeover token to anyone with log access.]

Open redirect via lane parameter — Phishing via trusted-domain redirect to attacker-controlled site [verified: RedirectResponse(lane) redirects to a fully attacker-controlled URL with no scheme/host validation.]

Mass assignment in ops workset endpoint — Attacker can set arbitrary role/tier/approved/balance values on the returned workset [verified: Duplicate of idx 9 — mass assignment on workset dict including role/tier/approved/balance.]

Reflected CORS origin with credentials allowed — Cross-origin attacker site can read authenticated responses using victim's credentials [verified: Origin header reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Allow-Credentials: true, enabling any origin to make credentialed requests.]

CSV formula injection in export endpoints — Formula injection payload embedded in a user-controlled name field executes when a manager/admin opens the exported rent-roll/maintenance/inspection CSV in a spreadsheet application, enabling data exfiltration or arbitrary command execution via DDE/macro-based formulas. [verified: full_name and other user-controlled fields flow unsanitized into csv.DictWriter.writerows with no escaping of leading =,+,-,@, confirming CSV/formula injection when opened in spreadsheet software.]

CSV formula injection in maintenance export — A malicious ticket title (e.g. "=cmd|'/c calc'!A1") opened in Excel/Sheets by an admin can trigger formula execution, leading to local code execution or data exfiltration on the analyst's machine. [verified: writer.writerows(data) at exports.py:105 writes ticket title/category directly with no escaping of leading =,+,-,@; both fields are attacker-controlled via ticket creation, causing formula injection when opened in spreadsheet software.]

CSV formula injection in inspections export — A crafted property/inspector name containing a leading formula character results in formula execution when the exported CSV is opened in spreadsheet software, enabling local code execution against the exporting user. [verified: writer.writerows(data) at exports.py:151 writes property/inspector names directly with no escaping of formula-trigger characters; these are user-settable free-text fields reaching the CSV sink unsanitized.]

Weak MD5 hash usage for sensitive digest — MD5 is broken for integrity/security purposes; collisions and preimage weaknesses undermine any security use of this digest [verified: hashlib.md5 used for a 'digest' of user-supplied phrase; broken hash function, though usage context has limited security impact.]

Weak PRNG used for nonce/token generation — Predictable tokens/nonces enabling brute-force or prediction attacks [verified: random.choice is non-cryptographic PRNG used to build a 'code'/nonce value, unlike secrets module used elsewhere.]
